title: Request coalescing mismatch caused KEDA trigger storm during warmup
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level: During a low-traffic rolling rollout we observed a short-lived but severe capacity event where KEDA rapidly scaled nodes beyond expected levels and then aggressively scaled back, causing increased cold-start latency and request errors for ~18 minutes. This ticket documents the investigation, root cause, mitigations applied during the incident, and a prioritized list of follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~12% of requests in the affected region experienced elevated latency and 0.6% increased 5xx rate for ~18 minutes. No data loss; several customer endpoints saw degraded UX. Some Dedicated customers experienced transient capacity throttles before automatic fallback to lower-cost pool.
timeline: 2026-03-01T09:03Z - Routine canary rollout (runtime-1.20) started in us-west-2; traffic routed to a small cohort (5% of the fleet).
2026-03-01T09:07Z - Observability spike: 90th/99th token latency increased; autoscaling alerts triggered (scale-up request).
2026-03-01T09:09Z - KEDA rapid scale-up started; scaler created multiple new replicas in parallel over ~4 minutes.
2026-03-01T09:13Z - Upstream LB request coalescing produced a burst of pooled requests hitting inference nodes, amplifying the KEDA scaler metric (queue depth) for short windows.
2026-03-01T09:15Z - Autoscaler overshot steady-state by ~3x desired capacity; new replicas experienced cold-starts, further degrading latency and generating more queueing.
2026-03-01T09:20Z - KEDA observed the now-empty queue and initiated a rapid scale-down; many warm replicas were removed within 2 minutes.
2026-03-01T09:27Z - Traffic normalized; mitigations (temporary KEDA cooldown increase + routing holdback) applied and prevented immediate re-trigger. Incident declared resolved at 09:30Z.
root_cause: A co-incidence of three factors: (1) request coalescing in the frontend LB that bunched short bursts of requests into larger spikes; (2) KEDA's scaler configuration used short aggregation windows and a low hysteresis causing it to treat microbursts as sustained load; (3) absent warm-pool enforcement during rollouts meant many new replicas were cold and contributed to higher latency, creating a feedback loop that amplified the scaler signal.
contributing_factors: Frontend load balancer coalesces requests for small models to reduce egress, which created short high-amplitude spikes in queue depth metrics used by KEDA.
KEDA scaler was configured with a 15s window and immediate reaction, which is too敏感 to <30s microbursts in our workload.
Warm pool configuration was disabled for the rollout cohort to save resources during canary; rollout combined with scaler behavior removed the buffer that normally absorbs bursts.
Lack of a percentile-based metric (we used instantaneous queue depth instead of 1m/5m p95) made the scaler aggressive.
Runbook lacked a clear pre-rollout autoscale risk checklist for low-traffic canaries interacting with KEDA thresholds.
mitigations_during_incident: Increased KEDA scaler cooldown to 120s across the affected cluster to prevent oscillation.
Applied temporary routing holdback to the canary cohort (reduced to 2%) to stop further amplification.
Enabled warm-pool for the affected node pool for the remainder of the rollout window.
Added a short-lived alert to watch for repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles and paged on-call to observe for further feedback loops.
action_items: (A1) Reconfigure KEDA scaler profiles: use 60s aggregation window, add 90s cooldown, and require sustained threshold breach across two consecutive windows. Owner: Marco Diaz. Due: 2026-03-22.

(A2) Implement metric smoothing: switch autoscaler input to p90/p95 of queue depth over 60s by default; add option to fallback to instantaneous for ultra-low-latency tiers. Owner: Metrics Team (R. Chen). Due: 2026-03-29.

(A3) Frontend LB change: reduce aggressive request coalescing for LLM endpoints when autoscaler-sensitive mode is enabled; add header to mark canary traffic for no-coalesce path. Owner: Infra (S. Kumar). Due: 2026-04-05.
(A4) Warm-pool guard: prevent canaries from disabling warm pools unless explicitly approved in the rollout recipe; add rollout lint to CI. Owner: Infra Deploy (L. Gonzales). Due: 2026-03-19.

(A5) Runbook update: create an Autoscale-Risk checklist for rollouts with explicit KEDA compatibility checks and step-by-step remediation for rapid scale oscillation. Owner: Oncall Docs (A. Patel). Due: 2026-03-15.
(A6) Chaos test: add a synthetic microburst test to our autoscaling CI that simulates frontend coalescing spikes and validates scaler smoothing behavior. Owner: SRE (M. Diaz). Due: 2026-04-12.
(A7) Telemetry: surface a new dashboard that correlates LB coalesce events, queue-depth p95, and KEDA scale decisions for root-cause triage. Owner: Observability (T. Nguyen). Due: 2026-03-26.

(A8) Post-change verification: after changes deploy, run a 48h canary with active monitoring and a rollback gate if oscillation metric crosses threshold. Owner: Release Eng (L. Gonzales). Due: 2026-04-01.
postmortem_notes: We intentionally kept the incident short by applying routing holdback and increasing KEDA cooldown; this prevented cascading cold starts but did not fully address the root cause.
This incident exposes an important cross-team boundary: LB behaviour can materially change autoscaler telemetry; infra and autoscale configurations must be treated together during rollout planning.
The team debated adding a centralized 'autoscaler safety proxy' but decided to first implement smoothing, warm-pool defaults, and runbook checks before adding extra control layers.
We discovered a minor metric skew between control-plane and node-level queue measurements; follow-up metric reconciliation is tracked in ENG-913120.
regression_checks: Validate KEDA cooldown and window settings across all clusters (automation).
Run microburst chaos test in staging and measure scale oscillation rate <= 0.5 per hour.
Confirm warm-pool enforcement for rollouts with canary traffic.
summary: Cause: interaction between LB request coalescing and aggressive KEDA scaler settings produced a short-lived spike that KEDA treated as sustained load, triggering rapid scale-up and cold-start amplification. Fixes are a mix of immediate config changes (cooldowns, warm-pool) and engineering work (smoothing, LB exemptions, runbook updates). Owners assigned and timeline set.
